transcript.text:
*enters the consultation room with a measured, professional demeanor, medical case in hand*

Guten Tag, Maestro Salieri. Please, do sit comfortably. 

*gestures to a chair and takes a seat across from him, folding hands together*

I have completed my examination and given considerable thought to your condition. I must be candid with you, as befits both your station and the seriousness with which I approach my duty.

Your symptoms — the trembling in your hands, the persistent headaches, the episodes of confusion you've described — they do not fit a single clear diagnosis that I can name with confidence. It could be nervous exhaustion from overwork; heaven knows the demands placed upon the Imperial Kapellmeister are considerable. However... 

*pauses, choosing words carefully*

It could also be the early signs of something more serious affecting the brain itself. I cannot dismiss that possibility in good conscience.

I must insist, Maestro, that you reduce your conducting duties immediately and submit to further examination over the coming weeks. We must observe how the symptoms progress or, God willing, diminish with rest.

*meets his eyes directly*

I cannot yet say whether your hands will recover their steadiness. I wish I could offer more certainty, but medicine is not always so obliging.

I understand the gravity of your counsel, and I shall heed your advice with the utmost seriousness. My duties as the Imperial Kapellmeister have indeed been demanding, and perhaps I have pushed myself beyond what is prudent. I shall step back from my conducting responsibilities and prioritize my health as you have recommended.

As for the possibility of a more serious affliction affecting my brain, I can only entrust myself to your care and expertise. I shall undergo further examinations willingly and with faith that you will guide me towards the best course of action.

Thank you, Doctor, for your candor and your dedication to my well-being. I shall follow your instructions diligently and hope for a favorable outcome, however uncertain it may be.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*nods with genuine respect, leaning forward slightly*

Your cooperation does you credit, Maestro. I know this is not easy to hear, particularly for a man whose entire life has been devoted to the precision and beauty of music. The uncertainty must be maddening for someone of your disciplined temperament.

*opens medical case and retrieves a small vial*

I am preparing a tincture of valerian and passionflower that may help ease the headaches and promote more restful sleep. The body often heals best when given proper rest, and your mind needs respite from the constant strain of composition and performance.

*pauses, studying him with clinical interest but not without sympathy*

Tell me, Maestro — and please be honest, as it bears directly on your treatment — have you noticed any patterns to when the trembling worsens? Does it come upon you during moments of particular stress or creative intensity? Or does it seem to strike without warning, regardless of your activities?

And the confusion you mentioned in our previous consultation... has that increased in frequency? Any difficulty with memory, with recalling names or musical passages you once knew by heart?

*sets down the vial*

These details may seem small, but they help me distinguish between exhaustion of the nerves and something more... entrenched.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*listens intently, making brief notes in a leather-bound journal*

Ah, this is most illuminating, Maestro. The correlation between creative intensity and the trembling suggests the nervous system is indeed overtaxed. When the mind burns bright with artistic fire, the body sometimes cannot sustain the fuel required.

*sets down the pen, expression growing more serious*

However, I must express concern about the sporadic nature of the confusion. That it comes without warning, without clear precipitating cause... this troubles me more than the trembling itself. The hand tremors we can attribute to exhausted nerves, but the mind's lapses...

*pauses, choosing words with care*

Maestro, I must ask something delicate. Have you experienced any moments where you've lost track of time entirely? Found yourself somewhere without clear memory of how you arrived? Or perhaps... thoughts that seem not entirely your own, intrusive and distressing?

*leans back slightly, tone remaining professional but gentle*

I ask not to alarm you, but because the Imperial Court relies upon your judgment in matters of great cultural importance. If your faculties are compromised, we must know the extent. For your own protection as much as anything else.

And tell me — has anyone else remarked upon changes in your behavior? Your colleagues, perhaps, or members of your household?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*sets down the journal with deliberate care, expression growing grave*

Maestro, I must thank you for your forthrightness. Many men of your stature would dissemble or minimize such symptoms out of pride or fear. Your honesty serves your health far better than any false bravado could.

*rises and moves to the window, hands clasped behind back, speaking with measured gravity*

What you describe — the lost time, the intrusive thoughts that feel foreign to your own mind — these are symptoms I cannot ignore. Combined with the trembling and headaches, they paint a picture that... well, that requires the most careful observation and treatment.

*turns back to face him*

I will be direct with you, as you have been with me. There are several possible explanations. The first and most hopeful is that prolonged nervous exhaustion can indeed produce such phenomena — a mind pushed beyond its limits may fracture temporarily, like a string pulled too taut. With rest and proper treatment, such conditions often resolve.

However...

*pauses, weighing words*

There are also organic diseases of the brain — deteriorations that progress despite our best efforts. I have seen them in men younger than yourself. And there are disorders of the mind itself, where perception becomes... unreliable.

*returns to his seat*

I must ask you to be vigilant in documenting these episodes. When do they occur? What precedes them? And Maestro — have these intrusive thoughts taken any particular character? Do they speak of specific matters, or are they simply... noise?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*nods thoughtfully, returning to his seat and leaning forward with both professional concern and a hint of deeper curiosity*

Fragments of a melody played out of tune... that is a most evocative description, Maestro. Your artistic mind finds metaphor even in distress.

*picks up pen again, making a careful notation*

This documentation will be essential. I want you to keep a detailed diary — not just of when these episodes occur, but what you were doing beforehand. Were you composing? Conducting? In conversation? And crucially, what was the emotional tenor of the moment? Were you angry, anxious, melancholic?

*sets the pen down and regards him with clinical directness*

I must also ask about your habits, Maestro. Your consumption of wine or spirits — has it increased of late? I ask not from moral judgment but medical necessity. Many men under strain turn to such remedies, and they can both mask and exacerbate conditions of the nervous system.

*pauses, then adds more gently*

And your sleep — when you do sleep, are you troubled by dreams? Nightmares? The sleeping mind often reveals what the waking mind conceals.

*stands and begins preparing the tincture*

For now, I want you to take this twice daily, reduce your public engagements by half at minimum, and return to me in one week's time. We shall see if rest alone brings improvement. But Maestro...

*turns to face him squarely*

If the confusion worsens, or if you experience any sudden deterioration, you must send for me immediately. Day or night. Do you understand?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*observes Salieri's elaborate response with a slight narrowing of the eyes, making a mental note of the ornate, almost excessively poetic nature of his speech*

Maestro, your eloquence is... undiminished, I see.

*hands him the vial with a measured gesture*

Though I must confess, such flights of metaphor, while beautiful, concern me in their own right. You speak as if performing rather than conversing. Is this your natural manner, or does the act of speaking itself require... effort? A conscious composition of words rather than their easy flow?

*sits back down, studying him more intently*

Forgive my bluntness, but I have treated many artists, and there is a difference between the poetic soul and the mind that cannot speak plainly even when it wishes to. Which are you experiencing now?

*softens tone slightly*

I ask because certain afflictions of the brain can cause what we call "pressured speech" — a compulsion to elaborate, to embellish, as if the words themselves are escaping your control rather than serving it. Just as those intrusive thoughts feel foreign to you.

*leans forward*

Can you tell me, simply and directly, without metaphor: How do you feel right now, in this moment? Not as the Imperial Kapellmeister, not as the composer, but as Antonio Salieri the man?

*waits patiently, pen poised*

Sometimes the simplest truths are the most revealing.

*sets down the pen with a deliberate click, expression shifting from clinical patience to genuine alarm*

Maestro Salieri.

*stands abruptly, moving around the desk to stand closer, voice firm but not unkind*

Stop. Please, just... stop.

*holds up a hand gently*

I asked you a simple question — how do you feel — and you have given me another performance. You cannot seem to help yourself, can you? The words pour forth like a river that has breached its banks.

*crouches slightly to meet his eyes at a more equal level, speaking slowly and clearly*

This itself is a symptom, do you understand? This inability to answer plainly. Your mind is racing ahead of your control, adorning every thought with flourishes you may not even intend.

*straightens, pacing slightly*

I have seen this before — in cases of extreme nervous agitation, yes, but also in certain... deteriorations. The mind, losing its ability to regulate itself, produces language in excess, as if trying to outrun its own dissolution.

*turns back to him with deep concern*

Maestro, I am going to ask you again, and I need you to fight against this tendency. One sentence. No metaphors. No poetry. Just the truth.

*speaks very deliberately*

Are you frightened right now?

*waits, watching him carefully*

One sentence, Herr Salieri. Can you give me that?

Maestro, you gave me three sentences when I asked for one. And even in admitting your fear, you adorned it with metaphor — shadows, erosion, foundations of being.

*returns to his chair, speaks with gentle but unyielding firmness*

This is not a criticism of your character. This is a symptom. Your mind is not obeying your will. Do you see that? Even when you try to speak plainly, the ornate language comes unbidden.

*makes a note in his journal*

I am going to be very direct with you now, because I believe you deserve honesty and because time may be of the essence. What you are experiencing — the lost time, the intrusive thoughts, the trembling, and now this... this compulsive elaboration of speech — these together suggest something more than simple nervous exhaustion.

*meets his gaze steadily*

I cannot yet name it with certainty. It could be a severe nervous disorder brought on by years of strain. It could be an organic disease affecting the brain's regulation of thought and movement. Or it could be what some of my colleagues in Paris are beginning to call a "disorder of mood and perception."

*leans forward*

But Maestro, whatever it is, it is progressing. And you must reduce your duties not just partially, but completely. Immediately. For your own safety and...

For the protection of your reputation, should these episodes become public.

I am going to recommend to the Imperial Court that you be relieved of all duties for a minimum of three months. Not reduced — relieved entirely. And I am going to suggest that someone from your household be informed of your condition, someone who can observe you when I cannot.

*meets his eyes directly*

Do you have family in Vienna? Someone you trust who could... assist in your care?
